figures.title: Stable softmax: shift, exponentiate, normalize
figures.caption: One row of three scores, 2.0, 1.0 and 0.1, passes through the stable softmax. Subtracting the row maximum 2.0 gives 0, −1.0 and −1.9; exponentiating gives 1, 0.368 and 0.150, summing to 1.518; dividing gives 0.659, 0.242 and 0.099, the same shares as the unshifted softmax. The last two columns apply temperature before exponentiating: T = 0.5 concentrates the row to 0.864 on the leader, T = 2 flattens it to 0.502. Those columns and their entropies are illustrative, computed from the chapter's scores; the chapter prints the T = 1 shares and H ≈ 0.85 nats.
figures.alt: A 3 by 6 matrix. Each row is one key. Columns are the raw score s, the score after subtracting the row maximum, the exponential, and the normalized share at T = 1, T = 0.5 and T = 2. Row one: 2.0, 0, 1, 0.659, 0.864, 0.502. Row two: 1.0, −1.0, 0.368, 0.242, 0.117, 0.304. Row three: 0.1, −1.9, 0.150, 0.099, 0.019, 0.194. The note prints the sum 1.518 and the entropies 0.45, 0.85 and 1.03 nats against ln 3 = 1.10.

data.note: Row max 2.0; shifted scores 0, −1.0, −1.9; exponentials 1, 0.368, 0.150; sum 1.518; T = 1 shares 0.659, 0.242, 0.099. The T = 0.5 and T = 2 columns are illustrative, computed by dividing the scores by T before exponentiating. Entropy: 0.45, 0.85, 1.03 nats; ceiling ln 3 = 1.10.

figures.title: The first token is the only key every query can see
figures.caption: The causal mask makes column 0 visible to every row: the first token is the one position a head can always attend to when no visible key is a good match. Softmax cannot output "attend to nothing", so a head with surplus mass can dump it on that token. Xiao et al. (2023) called this the attention sink; remove the first token from the window and perplexity explodes.
figures.alt: An 8 by 8 causal score grid. Rows are queries, columns are keys. Filled cells are allowed pairs with j ≤ i; the upper triangle is masked. Column 0 is filled in every row, so the first token is visible to every query.

data.note: Column 0 is the first token. Under causal masking it is the only key visible to every query, so it is always available as a null key. Softmax must put its mass somewhere; many heads in pretrained models dump surplus mass there. Remove that token from the window and perplexity explodes.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to see why the first token is always available.

steps.label: Causal masking shows a query at i only keys 0 through i: the lower triangle.
Column 0 appears in every row, so the first token is the only key every query can see.

sources.note: Vaswani et al.; the scaled dot-product softmax and the 1/sqrt(d_k) factor.
Xiao et al., Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks; the first-token sink and the perplexity collapse when it is evicted.
Milakov and Gimelshein, Online normalizer calculation for softmax; the incremental row maximum used by tiled kernels.
